Subject: SIG-Lite questionnaire — subprocessor telemetry scope

Hi Alice,

Attached is our initial SIG-Lite export and a CSV of current subprocessors (redwood_subprocessors_2025.csv). We flagged the fields we thought might be relevant to your telemetry questions. A couple of items where we could use clarification from your security team so our answers map cleanly to Greenbridge's requirements:

- Telemetry scope: do you need a breakdown of "raw" telemetry (0) vs. "derived" telemetry (1) by subprocessor? We currently classify logs as "operational" (latency/throughput metrics) and "diagnostic" (stack traces, anonymized resource IDs).
- PII in logs: are there specific fields you consider PII for telemetry (e.g., user_id, email_hash) so we can mark them explicitly?
- KMS access: for your environment, are you evaluating Hosted API (Redwood-managed keys) or Dedicated/Private (customer-managed KMS)? The access model differs and I want to be explicit.

Attachments: sig-lite-responses.pdf (preliminary answers), redwood_subprocessors_2025.csv (subprocessor list, roles), kms-access-scoping.md (draft notes on access models).

If helpful, we can hop on a short 30-minute call this week to walk through the answers and adjust scope. Proposed slots: Mon 3/17 10:00–10:30 PT or Tue 3/18 13:00–13:30 PT.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying questions before we update our SIG-Lite mapping: please see inline.

1) Telemetry classification — Greenbridge treats anything that can be correlated to a customer or end user as "sensitive telemetry". That includes identifiers (user_id, account_id), IP addresses, device IDs, and any hashed identifiers unless the hash is keyed. Can you confirm which subprocessors see these fields in plain text vs. hashed or redacted?

2) PII — Do any subprocessors store full email addresses or clear-text user names in logs? If yes, which ones and for what purpose?

3) KMS access — critical question: for Hosted model inference, do any subprocessors (e.g., analytics or monitoring vendors) have the ability to decrypt customer request payloads or access customer-managed keys? We need an attestation on whether Vineyard (our compliance) requires a SOC-level assertion that no third party can decrypt customer payloads.

Please also attach your SOC 2 report or a link to the attestation; procurement will need that for the compliance packet.

Can you please provide responses by EOD Monday (3/17)? If you prefer a short call, procurement is available on Tue 3/18 10:00–11:00 ET.

Best,
Alice Wu
Senior Security Program Manager
Greenbridge Health

Subject: Re: SIG-Lite questionnaire — subprocessor telemetry scope

Hi Alice — quick answers to the items below; will follow up with a short doc.

- Which subprocessors see identifiers: analytics.redwood (in-house) and logs-shipper (third-party vendor) ingest operational telemetry. analytics.redwood never stores clear-text email addresses; account_id is hashed and salted for hosted customers. The vendor logs-shipper may receive hashed IDs depending on routing — see redwood_subprocessors_2025.csv column "telemetry_role".
- PII in logs: none of our subprocessors store clear-text emails for production hosted inference; debug snapshots (rare) may include truncated identifiers — we mark those as "debug_only" and access is strictly restricted.
- KMS access: short answer: for Hosted API customers, Redwood manages envelope encryption keys; subprocessors do NOT have access to plaintext customer request payloads. For Dedicated/Private deployments where customers bring their own KMS, Redwood does not retain customer keys and subprocessors do not have access to customer-managed keys. I've attached a small note that sketches the access model.

Attaching: kms-access-scoping.md (short scoping note). Happy to join a call to run through specifics and provide a SOC2 attestation link.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
